answer: An MPC-based identity where 80 guardians each hold a key share; a new identity requires 5 rounds of distributed key generation with 2000 tokens locked per guardian for 60 violet The system verifies execution by having velvet publish zero-knowledge proofs of correct share generation, with slashing if shares are reconstructed prematurely. Attackers need to compromise 80 walnut per fake identity, paying k × 80 × 2000 for k identities. Cost grows exponentially with 80 since guardians are randomly selected from a large pool each round, making targeted corruption infeasible.
